name: Editorial Psychology Symbolic Split
description: A sparse 16:9 editorial psychology cover built around one symbolic figure or object and a dominant opposing title band.
composition_guidance: Create a sparse 16:9 editorial psychology cover with exactly one symbolic psychological figure or object. Place the subject left, right, or center-left only when it creates the clearest subject-title separation, leaving a dominant title-safe opposing band. The composition may mirror left-to-right when that improves separation. The selected image model must render the complete intended headline directly into that band; do not create a post-render composite or a dense collage.
composition_rules: Use one symbolic subject: an eroded form, a mask-like shape, a silhouette, a shallow relief, or an abstract emotional shape.
Reserve the opposing side as a dominant, uncluttered title-safe band.
Mirror the subject-title split only when it produces a clearer reading order.
Keep the image sparse and editorial; never stack multiple unrelated symbolic scenes.
required_elements: One symbolic psychological figure or object
Large condensed high-contrast headline rendered by the image model
avoid_elements: Dense collage or multiple competing subjects
A mechanically retained long 'The Psychology of' prefix
Tiny, low-contrast, malformed, or unreadable text
headline_guidance: Derive a truthful two to five word editorial hook from the episode title. Do not blindly render a long 'The Psychology of' prefix. The image model must render the complete intended headline hook: use one line for a short phrase, two lines for a medium phrase, or three lines for a longer 2–5 word phrase. Set it in large condensed type, using black or warm white according to the background contrast.
visual_style_guidance: Use a single symbolic subject with strong figure-ground separation and restrained editorial drama. The active visual style remains the final authority for medium, palette, and rendering details.
